# utf8h_1: submission package (generated by `leakproof package`; nothing has been posted)

> **Verified, needs human review.** Neither project tests nor a fuzz harness ran, so the gate saw only the reproducer (and any generated or adversary inputs). Read the diff before sending.

Issue: https://github.com/me7alix/utf8.h/issues/1
Defect: global-buffer-overflow in `utf8_decode` (`utf8.h:37`). Gate verdict: **verified**; evidence: verified, needs human review.

**Partial fix.** Not fixed here: overlong encodings, surrogates and non-continuation bytes are still accepted (the issue's other requests).

## The patch

`0001-utf8-fix-global-buffer-overflow-in-utf8-decode.patch` (this directory), `git format-patch` form: apply with `git am 0001-utf8-fix-global-buffer-overflow-in-utf8-decode.patch`. The
author is `<your git identity>` unless `--author` was given; fix it with
`git commit --amend --reset-author`.

```diff
diff --git a/utf8.h b/utf8.h
--- a/utf8.h
+++ b/utf8.h
@@ -19,12 +19,20 @@
 
 	if ((p[0] & 0xE0) == 0xC0) {
 		*bytes_read = 2;
+		if (p[1] == 0) {
+			*bytes_read = 1;
+			return 0xFFFD;
+		}
 		return ((p[0] & 0x1F) << 6) |
 		       (p[1] & 0x3F);
 	}
 
 	if ((p[0] & 0xF0) == 0xE0) {
 		*bytes_read = 3;
+		if (p[1] == 0 || p[2] == 0) {
+			*bytes_read = 1;
+			return 0xFFFD;
+		}
 		return ((p[0] & 0x0F) << 12) |
 		       ((p[1] & 0x3F) << 6) |
 		       (p[2] & 0x3F);
@@ -32,6 +40,10 @@
 
 	if ((p[0] & 0xF8) == 0xF0) {
 		*bytes_read = 4;
+		if (p[1] == 0 || p[2] == 0 || p[3] == 0) {
+			*bytes_read = 1;
+			return 0xFFFD;
+		}
 		return ((p[0] & 0x07) << 18) |
 		       ((p[1] & 0x3F) << 12) |
 		       ((p[2] & 0x3F) << 6) |
```

## Planner's analysis (written before the fix; check it against the diff)

Nemotron 3 Ultra wrote this root-cause analysis before any patch existed. It can describe a
different mechanism than the one the final diff fixes, so it is here for the reviewer and never
in the commit message.

> The `utf8_decode` function determines the UTF-8 sequence length from the first byte's prefix bits but does not verify that the input buffer actually contains the required continuation bytes before reading p[1], p[2], p[3]. On a truncated or malformed sequence at the end of a buffer, this reads past the allocated memory, causing a global-buffer-overflow.
